name: Technical
description: Programming, AI/ML, engineering, cloud, DevOps, cybersecurity and other hands-on technical subjects.

sections.label: Introduction
sections.guidance: Open with why this chapter matters and what problem it solves. 2-3 short paragraphs, no fluff.

sections.label: Learning Objectives
sections.guidance: 3-6 measurable objectives starting with an action verb (implement, configure, evaluate).

sections.label: Concept
sections.guidance: Define the core concepts precisely. Introduce terminology explicitly before using it.

sections.label: How It Works
sections.guidance: Explain the mechanism step by step: inputs, processing, outputs, failure modes.

sections.label: Visual Explanation
sections.guidance: Add a diagram only when the structure or data flow is genuinely hard to describe in words.

sections.label: Technical Example
sections.guidance: A concrete worked example with realistic values. Explain the example before and after showing it.

sections.label: Code Example
sections.guidance: Only when the topic involves code. Runnable, idiomatic, commented, with the language set correctly.

sections.label: Step-by-Step Implementation
sections.guidance: Ordered, reproducible steps a learner can follow on their own machine or cloud account.

sections.label: Common Mistakes
sections.guidance: Real mistakes practitioners make, each with the symptom and the fix.

sections.label: Best Practices
sections.guidance: Actionable, current practices. Avoid vague advice like 'follow best practices'.

sections.label: Exercise
sections.guidance: A hands-on task with clear instructions, hints and a verifiable expected outcome.

sections.label: Challenge
sections.guidance: A harder, open-ended extension for confident learners.

sections.label: Quiz
sections.guidance: 3-5 questions that test understanding rather than recall. Include the answer and a short explanation.

sections.label: Summary
sections.guidance: Key takeaways plus what the next chapter builds on.

writer_guidance: Write for practitioners. Be precise and concrete: name real tools, versions, commands and trade-offs. Prefer short paragraphs over walls of text. Never invent APIs, benchmark numbers, or citations. Use code blocks for anything a learner would type. Depth over breadth - it is better to explain three things properly than nine things vaguely.
research_guidance: Prioritise authoritative and current sources: official documentation, specifications, well-known engineering blogs and papers. Capture exact terminology, version-specific behaviour, common failure modes and performance characteristics.
review_focus: technical correctness of every claim, command and code sample
code quality: runnable, idiomatic, safe defaults, no deprecated APIs
no invented sources, statistics or benchmarks
progression from prerequisites to advanced material
image_guidance: Prefer clean architecture, data-flow or sequence diagrams on a light background. Minimal, legible labels. Flat vector style, no photorealism, no decorative clutter, no fake UI screenshots.

theme.font_family: Inter, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
